nodes.name: Coprecipitation of AP NiFe LDH
nodes.procedure: A 10 ml of aqueous solution containing 0.075 M NiCl2·6H2O (≥98%, Sigma-Aldrich, Australia) and 0.025 M FeCl3·6H2O (97%, Sigma-Aldrich, Australia) was added dropwise to 20 ml of formamide (≥99%, Sigma-Aldrich, Australia) solution (23 vol.%) under magnetic stirring at 80°C. The solution pH was simultaneously maintained at 9−10 with dropwise adding 0.25 M NaOH (≥98%, Sigma-Aldrich, Australia). The reaction was completed within 10 min.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of E NiFe LDH on Ti mesh
nodes.procedure: The electrodeposition was performed initially in a standard three-electrode setup with a Ti mesh (1×1 cm; Alibaba.com, China) working electrode, a graphite rod counter electrode, and an Ag/AgCl (saturated KCl) reference electrode. A 30 mL aqueous solution containing 0.06 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (≥97.0%, Sigma-Aldrich, Australia) and 0.048 M Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (≥98%, Sigma-Aldrich, Australia) was used as electrolyte. The electrodeposition potential was kept at −1.0 V vs. Ag/AgCl for 100 s.
nodes.source_text: The electrodeposition was performed initially in a standard three-electrode setup with a Ti mesh... The electrodeposition potential was kept at −1.0 V vs. Ag/AgCl for 100 s.

nodes.name: Anion exchange for E NiFe LDH-[PO43-]
nodes.procedure: The Ti meshes after electrodeposition were washed using deionized (DI) water (Milli-Q EQ 7000, 18.2 MΩ cm), and then immersed in 5 mL of aqueous solutions containing 1 M NaOH and 0.1 M Na3PO4, respectively, in sealed bottles for 12 h at room temperature.

nodes.description: Corrosion polarization curves in alkaline saline on Ti foil (Fig. 2e)
nodes.source_text: Electrochemical measurements shown in Fig. 2e were performed using a typical three-electrode setup with alkaline saline as electrolyte... 50 μL of NiFe LDH-[A] ink was dropped onto a Ti foil (0.5 × 1.5 cm) as working electrode. The corrosion polarized curve was firstly obtained at a scanning rate of 5 mV s−1, and then transferred to Tafel plots by taking the logarithm of current density.

nodes.description: CP tests in two-electrode setup alkaline seawater
nodes.source_text: AP NiFe LDH-based anode exhibited good resistance to Cl− and stability at current densities lower than 0.5 A cm−2, it suffered from severe electrode corrosion and ClER as the current density increased to higher levels (Figs. 3a and S12).

nodes.description: CP tests in two-electrode setup alkaline seawater
nodes.source_text: NiFe LDH-[PO₄³⁻]-based anode displayed a significant improvement in both OER activity and corrosion resistance; it demonstrated more stable operation across various current densities ranging from 0.1 to 1.5 A cm−2.
the target ASWE achieved a high current density of 1.0 A cm−2 at a low cell voltage of about 2.0 V... Notably, the target ASWE worked stably at 1.0 A cm−2 for over 1000 hours.

the NiFe LDH-[PO₄³⁻]-based ASWE demonstrated higher energy efficiency (EE), calculated based on the higher heating value (HHV) of hydrogen... It achieved 73.4% EE at 0.5 A cm−2 at about 2.0 V... Notably, the target ASWE exhibited stable operation for 100 hours at a high current density of 0.5 A cm−2... During the duration test, about 2.24 Nm³, equivalent to 0.2 kg, of pure hydrogen was produced every 10 hours; about 8.6 g of KOH was consumed per kilogram seawater for Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ precipitation treatment.
The commercial Raney Ni-based AWE achieved a current density of 0.2 A cm−2 at about 2.0 V using pure 6 M KOH as electrolyte.
